result.rationale: The migration inserts old site-setting values verbatim via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '') ... `) that strips scheme/path. Yet `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = uri.host`, so an existing entry like 'https://example.com/1234' is copied unchanged and will never match the bare hostname — and since the migration deletes the site settings, the authorization is permanently lost. This is a real data/backfill defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 copies host values directly from the old site_settings table with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The old embeddable_hosts setting could contain entries like 'http://example.com' or 'https://example.com/path'. However, the new EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has a before_validation callback that strips 'http://' and paths, and the host_allowed? method compares against URI(host).host. The migration doesn't apply this normalization, so migrated entries with schemes/paths will be stored verbatim but won't match during lookup since the comparison uses the parsed hostname only.
